name: Consent log (evidence-grade consent records)
observed_behavior: A searchable, exportable table of 48,920 consent records with summary strip (total, accepted 78%, rejected 13%, customised 9%), columns Consent ID / Date & Time / Country / Decision / Categories / Framework / IP (masked) / Device, framework values spanning GDPR, CCPA, LGPD, PIPEDA, APPI, Privacy Act; pagination to 5,436 pages; Export CSV action; filters for period, website, decision.
unverified_behavior: Collection mechanics, retention, proof-of-consent storage, deletion workflows.
business_problem: Regulators and auditors require per-visitor consent evidence, not aggregate claims.
jobs_to_be_done: Prove what a visitor consented to, when, under which framework; export evidence.
actions: Search by ID/IP, filter, Export CSV, paginate
input_fields: Period, website, decision filters; search text
audit: The log itself is the audit artefact
data_entities: ConsentRecord {id, ts, country, decision, categories[], framework, ip_masked, device}
automation_candidates: Anomaly alert when rejection rate spikes per framework
edge_cases: Scale (48,920 rows shown) demands server pagination + export jobs, never client rendering of full sets
security_privacy: IP handling is personal-data processing: masking, retention limits and access logging required
benefit_hypothesis: Evidence-grade logs turn compliance from assertion into proof.
acceptance_criteria: Given 48,920 records, when an auditor filters by framework=GDPR and exports, then a CSV job is created and the export contains only matching records with masked IPs.
test_cases: IP masking in UI and export
